notes: 1 section header — too few for a contents list.
2057 words with no section headers at all — the biggest single improvement available here.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a real heading
decisions.why: "Family Links" is a paragraph in bold type. It reads as a heading and is spaced like one, but it is not in the page's outline, a screen reader does not announce it, and the contents list cannot link to it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 1 heading is plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 372 links on this page open a file — 331 PDF, 41 PowerPoint — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 22 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Let a colon do its own work
decisions.why: A colon marks the words before it as a term and the words after it as what the term means. Here 4 list items open with a term set in the same weight as its own explanation, so the list cannot be scanned. 52 links sit immediately in front of a colon, where the chevron lands between the term and the punctuation that belongs to it. 52 format tags stand between a title and its description and move to the end of the row. No word changes and nothing is removed.
